newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan police kill three ethnic activists.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan police kill three ethnic activists.

text.p: Pakistani police said they had killed three armed members of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and wounded a fourth in a shoot-out on Monday in the troubled port city of Karachi.
The three men, all in their early 20s, were killed in a gunbattle with police in the volatile eastern Korangi area, while one was wounded, the police said.
"These boys, all belonging to the MQM, had barged into a house in Korangi for a robbery," Inspector Rustom Khattak of Korangi police station told Reuters.
"There was an exchange of fire between the police and these armed men for around 20 minutes in which they were killed. While the fourth one saved himself by hiding under a pile of sheets," he said.
He said a Kalashnikov assault rifle and two pistols were seized from the "robbers".
MQM officials said they had no details of the incident.

The MQM speaks for Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India at Partition in 1947 and their descendants. It is a coalition partner in the government of the Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party.
More than 155 people have been killed in political and sectarian violence in Karachi in the last four months compared to more than 500 in 1996 and more than 2,000 in 1995.
